themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it. So the models keep starting by building a small truth set of their own, or by admitting the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization the models say model drift outruns any change a brand makes, on identity resolution they say nobody has a verified list of who is really the same person, on B2B buying-group intent they say few accounts ever buy so a dead signal and a fake one look alike, and on incrementality they say the platforms control both the treatment and the evidence.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, a message, or a buying conversation leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, trained model, or private chat that now holds it. You can estimate whether the rules were honored, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion the models call ad platforms and agency segments black boxes with no accepted test for removal from a trained model, on B2B buying-group intent they say early evaluation happens in private channels no tag can reach, and on identity resolution they say false matches inside closed platforms cannot be measured without creating new privacy risk.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution all three models put a proxy or gateway in front of every write, take credentials away from agents, and cap spend and audience size, with one adding a dry-run diff; on downstream consent they route every data export through a single checkpoint, and on journey orchestration they make every channel check one shared contact ledger before sending.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the person holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The models increasingly try to make honesty pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic today all three models design a faster, cheaper lane for agents that declare themselves, and name liability for lying and spoofing incentives as the real blocker; on journey orchestration channel owners are paid to keep sending, and on the semantic context layer teams keep rival definitions of customer on purpose.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set fully captures that. The models end up shrinking human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance the models say deciding whether evidence supports a claim is a contextual judgment that expert reviewers themselves dispute, so they build an approved-claims library and limit what tools may write; on the semantic context layer they call one shared definition of customer a political settlement in a data modeling costume.
